contentBeforeToc:
India’s eCommerce market is growing at a tremendous speed, and it’s projected to reach around $325 billion by 2030. However, right now, thousands of Indian business owners are with the very same concern, prior to the launch: Shopify vs WooCommerce, which one is better?

So, let us mention that both platforms are powerful. Both can build a great online store. But they are built on completely different philosophies, and the wrong choice for your specific business can cost you money, time, and rankings down the line.

Through the medium of this guide, we’re gonna break down each and every critical factor, including pricing in INR, Indian payment gateways, SEO, ease of use, scalability, and more. Just so you can make better decisions for your business in India.
contentAfterToc:
Shopify vs WooCommerce: A Quick Overview

Shopify is a fully hosted, all-in-one eCommerce platform. You pay a monthly subscription, and Shopify handles everything hosting, security, updates, and infrastructure. You just built your store and are selling.

WooCommerce is a free, open-source plugin built on WordPress. It is not a standalone platform; it converts your WordPress website into a fully functional eCommerce store. You own and manage everything, from hosting to security to updates.

Here is a side-by-side snapshot for this eCommerce platform comparison India:

Feature Shopify WooCommerce
Type Hosted SaaS Self-hosted (WordPress)
Starting Cost ~₹2,400/month Free (hosting extra ~₹300–₹800/mo)
Ease of Use Beginner-friendly Moderate technical knowledge
Customization Limited (within the Shopify ecosystem) Unlimited (open-source)
Payment Gateway Third-party only in India Full flexibility, free plugins
Transaction Fees 2% on Basic (no Shopify Payments in India) No platform fees
SEO Control Basic to Moderate Advanced (via WordPress + Yoast)
Hosting Included in plan Self-managed required
Best For Fast launch, low maintenance Custom builds, content-heavy stores

Shopify vs WooCommerce Pricing in India

Pricing is where the Shopify vs WooCommerce decision gets real for most Indian businesses. Here is the full picture:

Shopify Plans in INR

  • Basic Shopify: ~₹2,400/month — unlimited products, 2
    staff accounts, basic reports
  • Shopify: ~₹6,600/month — professional reports, 5 staff
    accounts
  • Advanced Shopify: ~₹25,000/month — advanced reporting,
    15 staff accounts
  • Shopify Plus: ₹1,90,000+/month — enterprise features,
    custom checkout

Critical India flag: Shopify Payments is NOT available in India. This means you must use a third-party payment gateway (Razorpay, Cashfree, Paytm, etc.) on every plan. On the Basic plan, Shopify charges an additional 2% transaction fee on every sale — on top of the payment gateway’s own fee. This Shopify India transaction fee disappears only on the ₹6,600/month plan and above.

WooCommerce Cost Breakdown

  • WooCommerce plugin: Free
  • Hosting: ₹300–₹800/month
    (shared) to ₹3,000–₹8,000/month (managed WordPress hosting)
  • Domain:
    ₹700–₹1,500/year
  • Theme: ₹0 (free themes) to
    ₹5,000–₹15,000 (premium one-time)
  • Essential plugins (SEO, security, backup):
    ₹0–₹5,000/year

Bottom line on pricing: WooCommerce has a lower starting cost, but the total cost depends entirely on the hosting and plugins you choose. Shopify’s pricing is predictable but the 2% transaction fee on the Basic plan makes it expensive for high-volume Indian stores that cannot absorb that cost.

Payment Gateways: The Most Critical Factor for Indian
Businesses

In India, UPI is non-negotiable. If your store does not support GPay, PhonePe, or Paytm, you are leaving a massive chunk of Indian buyers behind. Here is how both platforms handle Indian payment gateways:

Shopify: Indian Payment Gateway Support

  • Supports Razorpay, Cashfree, Paytm, CCAvenue, and other Indian
    gateways via apps
  • Shopify Payments is NOT available in India. Every transaction goes
    through a third-party gateway
  • The basic plan charges an additional 2% transaction fee on top of
    the gateway fee
  • Razorpay on Shopify: works well, but adds the Shopify transaction
    fee on Basic

WooCommerce: Indian Payment Gateway Support

  • Free plugins available for Razorpay, Paytm, PhonePe, Cashfree,
    CCAvenue, and more
  • Zero platform transaction fees, you only pay the payment
    gateway’s own fee (typically 2% on Razorpay)
  • Full UPI support across all major gateways
  • Razorpay WooCommerce plugin: free, easy to install, widely used by
    Indian D2C brands

Winner for Indian payment flexibility: WooCommerce. No platform transaction fees and full freedom to integrate any Indian payment gateway make WooCommerce the stronger choice for cost-conscious Indian businesses, especially at the early growth stage.

Ease of Use: Shopify vs WooCommerce for Indian Businesses

For most Indian business owners, especially first-time eCommerce entrepreneurs, ease of use is a deciding factor. Here is how both platforms compare:

Shopify: Built for Non-Technical Users

  • Fully managed — no hosting, no security updates, no server
    management
  • Clean dashboard, guided setup, intuitive product management
  • App store for adding features — no coding required for most
    functions
  • Ideal for business owners who want to focus on selling, not managing
    infrastructure

WooCommerce: Requires More Technical Comfort

  • Requires WordPress installation, hosting setup, and plugin
    management
  • More control, but with more responsibility — updates, backups,
    security are on you
  • Steeper learning curve for non-technical users
  • Best suited for those with some WordPress familiarity or with a
    development partner

If you are a non-technical business owner launching your first store, Shopify’s simplicity is a genuine advantage. If you have a Shopify development partner handling your store setup and ongoing management, the technical gap disappears entirely.

SEO: Which Platform Wins for Indian Stores?

For Indian D2C brands investing in content marketing and organic search, Shopify vs WooCommerce SEO is a critical differentiator.

WooCommerce SEO Advantages

  • Built on WordPress, widely regarded as the most SEO-friendly CMS in
    the world
  • Full control over URL structure, meta tags, headings, and schema
    markup
  • Yoast SEO and Rank Math are best-in-class SEO plugins available for
    free
  • Superior blogging capabilities critical for content-heavy D2C Indian
    brands
  • No forced URL structures, full flexibility on permalink
    settings

Shopify SEO Limitations

  • Forced URL structures /collections/ and /products/ prefixes cannot
    be removed
  • Limited blog functionality basic compared to WordPress
  • Less granular SEO control compared to WooCommerce + Yoast
  • SEO apps available, but many are paid and overlap with free
    WooCommerce tools

Winner for SEO: WooCommerce, especially for Indian brands running content marketing alongside their store. If organic traffic and long-term SEO are priorities for your business, WooCommerce’s WordPress foundation gives you a significant edge.

If you need expert WooCommerce development to set up your store’s SEO architecture correctly from day one, that investment pays for itself quickly.

Scalability & Customization

As your Indian store grows, your platform needs to grow with it. Here is how both platforms handle scale and custom requirements:

Shopify Scalability Without Complexity

  • Handles traffic spikes reliably, no server management needed
  • Shopify Plus is designed for high-volume enterprise stores
  • App ecosystem covers most business needs without custom
    development
  • Limitation: deep customization requires
    Liquid knowledge or expensive custom apps

WooCommerce Unlimited Customization

  • Open-source any feature, any design, any integration is
    possible
  • Scales with the right hosting infrastructure (VPS or managed
    WordPress hosting)
  • Preferred by Indian D2C brands with complex product configurations,
    B2B requirements, or multilingual needs
  • Freedom to build custom features without platform
    restrictions

For the best eCommerce platform for Indian businesses that need deep customization — unique checkout flows, complex product configurations, B2B pricing, or regional language support WooCommerce wins. For Indian businesses that want to scale fast without technical overhead, Shopify is the stronger choice.

It is also worth noting that WooCommerce currently leads in India with 135,274 active stores vs Shopify’s 78,411, reflecting the Indian market’s preference for cost-effective, flexible solutions.

Shopify vs WooCommerce: Which Should You Choose?

There is no universal winner in the WooCommerce vs Shopify India debate. The right platform depends entirely on your business situation. Use this decision framework:

Your Situation Best Platform
You want a fast, hassle-free store launch ✅ Shopify
You are non-technical and want managed hosting ✅ Shopify
Budget is tight, and you want lower long-term costs ✅ WooCommerce
You want full SEO control and a content-heavy store ✅ WooCommerce
You need deep customization for a unique store ✅ WooCommerce
You are already on WordPress ✅ WooCommerce
You want to scale fast without managing servers ✅ Shopify
You need maximum Indian payment gateway flexibility ✅ WooCommerce

Choose Shopify if:

  • You want to launch fast with minimal technical setup
  • You are a non-technical founder who wants a fully managed
    platform
  • You are on a higher plan (₹6,600+/month) where the transaction
    fee is waived
  • You prioritize reliability and uptime over customization

Choose WooCommerce if:

  • You want lower long-term platform costs and zero transaction
    fees
  • SEO and content marketing are core to your growth strategy
  • You need deep customization, custom checkout, B2B features,
    multilingual support
  • You are already on WordPress or have a development partner to manage
    the setup

Final Thoughts

Simply put, the Shopify vs WooCommerce decision was never about which one is better and which one is not; rather, it’s about which one is more suitable for your specific business. Here, Shopify clearly has a win in simplicity and better infrastructure. On the other hand, WooCommerce will win on cost, SEO depth, and customization, especially if it’s about the Indian market, where payment gateway flexibility & zero transaction fees matter significantly.

Start by asking:

  • Do you want to manage your store’s infrastructure, or do you
    want someone else to?
  • Do you prioritize fast launch or long-term SEO?
  • What is your realistic monthly budget, including transaction
    fees?

FAQ

Is Shopify available in India?

Yes, Shopify is fully available in India. You can simply visit it, sign up, build your store, and sell to both Indian and international customers. However, Shopify Payments, Shopify’s native payment gateway, is not available in India, so you will need to integrate a third-party Indian payment gateway like Razorpay or Cashfree.

Is Shopify Payments available in India?

No. Shopify Payments is not available in India as of 2025. Indian merchants must use third-party payment gateways. On the Basic Shopify plan, this means paying an additional 2% transaction fee on every sale on top of the gateway’s own fee.

This Shopify India transaction fee is waived for the Shopify plan (₹6,600/month) and above.

Which is cheaper, Shopify or WooCommerce, for Indian
businesses?

WooCommerce has a lower starting cost since the plugin itself is free. With affordable Indian hosting (₹300–₹800/month), you can run a WooCommerce store for significantly less than Shopify’s Basic plan.

However, Shopify’s predictable pricing includes hosting, security, and support, so total cost depends on your store’s scale and technical requirements.

Does WooCommerce support Razorpay and UPI?

Yes. WooCommerce has a free official Razorpay plugin that supports UPI, cards, net banking, wallets, and EMI, all the payment methods Indian customers use. There are no platform transaction fees on WooCommerce, so you only pay Razorpay’s standard gateway fee.

Which platform is better for SEO in India?

WooCommerce wins for SEO, particularly for Indian brands investing in content marketing. Built on WordPress, WooCommerce gives you full control over URL structures, meta tags, schema markup, and blog content, amplified by powerful free plugins like Yoast SEO and Rank Math.

Shopify’s SEO is solid but more restricted, with forced URL structures and limited blog functionality.

Can I migrate from WooCommerce to Shopify?

Yes, migration from WooCommerce to Shopify is possible and involves transferring products, customer data, orders, and SEO redirects. It requires careful planning to avoid data loss and ranking drops. Similarly, migrating from Shopify to WooCommerce is also achievable.

Professional migration support ensures a smooth transition without disrupting your business or SEO performance.
